item.title: A Billion Tokens, Ten Thousand Fake Birds
item.description: The birding app Mingji had a strangely huge install package because its field-guide art came from an AI “global bird sticker” dump: more than 10,000 white-border stickers generated in a week by someone who is not a bird expert. The project mass-scraped field photos without permission, then added its own license and told unhappy photographers they could opt out within 7 days—birding communities say that doesn’t wash. The drawings get basic anatomy wrong, and AI-sharpened photos have already been uploaded to iNaturalist as science records. Compute is not expertise; pretty is not proof.

item.title: Anthropic's Messy Report on AI at Work
item.description: Anthropic interviewed people at 58 U.S. companies about working with AI. The new fight is over who owns the time AI saves. Workplace chaos includes “Claude grenades” (huge AI memos dumped on teammates), vibe-coded tools nobody maintains, and staff who hide their prompts. Mass layoffs are still rare, but two-thirds of firms hired less. Of clear gains, 55% went to company output and 19% to cost cuts; direct employee benefit was only 7%, and real extra rest just 1%. If workers don’t share the upside, they hide their tricks and go quiet.

item.title: After trying Herdr, Orca, T3 Code and Paseo, this is my full coordinator skill

item.title: Built a tiny model that recognizes user emotions from cursor movement
item.description: - Jakub Antalik 开发了一个轻量模型，可根据鼠标指针的移动速度和交互行为识别用户情绪，包括困惑、沮丧或迷失，并用于生成式或自适应界面。Beta 版可免费使用。 - 该模型在设备本地运行，不使用大语言模型或服务器，也不会让数据离开页面。它通过指针、点击、滚动和输入行为判断用户状态；目前已推出 React 版本，SwiftUI 和 React Native 版本即将推出。 - 模型每 250 毫秒评估一次用户状态，并结合快速动作信号为界面提供平滑的情绪强度读数。模型约 142 KB（gzip 后约 32 KB），无需网络请求。 - 初步测试中，模型在 60 个问题里识别出 48 个，平静时段误报率为 2.3%。已知局限包括可能漏掉短暂迷路，也可能把受阻的结账流程或频繁浏览区块误判为迷失。

item.title: How the Claude Code Team Thinks About Verification
item.description: About 90% of Claude Code's code is written and reviewed by Claude. Addy Osmani's engineering post argues that verification decides how many Claudes you can let run at once: without a verification loop you can watch one or two; with reliable checks you can run dozens. The three tests most worth investing in are end-to-end tests that give the agent eyes and hands, property tests that hammer an invariant with massive generated inputs, and differential tests that compare new and old systems. Six rules keep agents honest: run the real app, hand off to a human after three failed rounds, never let a change edit the rules that judge it, pick 3–10 checks from a 39-item reliability list based on the change, turn misses into hooks or CLAUDE.md rules, and observe new rules before enforcing them. Engineers shift from fixing code to setting the bar.

item.title: How T3 Code and Orca Make Multi-Agent Collaboration Seamless
item.description: @meow2149 reads the source of T3 Code and Orca and argues that spinning up many coding agents is easy; the hard part is delegation, communication, context handoff, and recovery after failure. Both add an orchestration layer on top of Codex, Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode. T3 Code uses MCP delegation and an event-driven runtime (delegate_task, an event store, and incremental AppThread/ProviderThread handoff). Orca uses a CLI protocol and a mailbox (worker-start; ask/reply/worker_done), models Task and Dispatch separately so stale results cannot overwrite state, and supports a task DAG. Both isolate parallel work with Git Worktree. The takeaway: this is starting to look like an OS for agents, and the real bar is division of labor, communication, waiting, handoff, and fault tolerance.

item.title: A Prompt to Help You Design the Meaning of Your Life
item.description: Kazike turns Stanford's Designing Your Life of Meaning into a multi-turn AI prompt. Meaning need not wait for success or a final answer; it lives in ordinary days. Life splits into a transaction world of outcomes and a flow world of experience. Instead of asking what the meaning of life is, ask how to create a little more meaning in the life you already have. The prompt walks through four stages—you are here, wonder and flow, your compass, live with a question—and delivers a Personal Meaning Design Handbook. After running it himself, the author realized that what had always felt most meaningful was creating.

item.description: Guicang's AIGC Weekly #198. Cubox only cached the opening and two featured items; the issue itself says the remaining 79% is paywalled and was not stored. item.title: When Design Experience Starts Evolving Itself: TaoDesign's Exploration and Practice
item.description: TaoDesign is Taotian's native AI design tool for real product delivery. A MasterGo plugin that mapped HTML/CSS onto canvas nodes reached about 85% first-pass usability, but lossy cross-format conversion became the bottleneck, so the team made the browser the board and treated HTML/JSX as the artifact. A client, server, and cloud sandbox stack applies deterministic patches first, with an agent as fallback and async snapshots for rollback. Design know-how is distilled into tokens, reusable structures, static assets, and business rules, then revised through offline evals and online feedback. Multi-state flows and node annotations travel with the mock via MCP to engineering and design QA.

item.title: Collie: Herd Your Agents from Your Phone
item.description: Collie is an open-source, self-hosted super agent by lihuanyu0w0. Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity sessions running on your computers can be watched and continued from your phone. Collie splits work by context, dispatches it in parallel, and only stops to ask when money, deletion, or shipping is involved; permission prompts become tap-to-reply cards. An always-on hub sits on a dev machine; other computers join with collie node over an outbound tunnel, with no open ports or SSH. Agents run inside herdr. It is a single Go binary plus SQLite, with the frontend embedded, and data stays on your machines.

item.title: Six Months of Agent Evals: Evaluation Is Product Engineering, Copying a Harness Won't Fix It
item.description: Kaiyi reviews six months of evaluation work on general agents such as Tabbit Browser, Offloop, and Persom. Model evals mostly need a well-defined problem; agent evals also have to define the solution, because prompts, tools, skills, and the harness are tightly coupled and cannot be split from product and engineering iteration. - Design scoring metrics first, then write tasks. Make observability the priority, own subjective judgments, and use both snapshot regression and daily live runs for time-sensitive work. - A harness will not be fully eaten by stronger models, and copying a framework will not fix the last mile: standing up a loop is easy, but every character is coupled, so you still have to understand and evaluate changes. Professional benchmarks lose meaning when audiences only look at scores and latency, or when "kill-line" screenshots oversimplify model capability.

item.title: cutaway: From One Picture to a Take-Apart 3D Mechanical Model
item.description: HeLi (@HeLi8866) highlights the open-source Claude Code skill cutaway (Nyxera0x/cutaway): give it one reference image and Claude rebuilds a detailed, take-apart 3D mechanical model in Three.js from code. He tested it with a ChatGPT render and the word "octopus," and got a 10-blade mechanical iris, a borosilicate glass dome that lifts and flips, and eight arms on a 48-tooth hub; the cutaway film drops a part every 3 seconds and is fully disassembled by about 19 seconds. The skill is MIT-licensed (~380 stars at capture) and was documented by @isagi1000x; install with npx skills add Nyxera0x/cutaway -g -a claude-code.

item.title: cospan: an async delegation protocol that lets coding agents orchestrate each other
item.description: - Cospan：让不同编码代理统一协作。 它通过异步委派协议连接 Antigravity、Codex、Claude Code、DeepSeek Harness 等工具。项目将“模型 × 执行环境”视为协作单元，代理可在后台派发任务、非阻塞地查看进度，并按需获取结果或完整执行记录。 - 核心用法与场景： 通过 /cospan-<harness>、Claude Code 中的 /cospan:<harness>，或 Codex 中的 $cospan:<harness> 指派任务，并可指定模型、推理强度和超时。支持并行代码审查、跨模型方案评估、浏览器与 GUI 测试、并发检查，以及从规划到审核的完整研究流程。Antigravity 和 DeepSeek Harness 还提供统一侧边栏，用于查看后台任务、问答结果和 Git worktree。 - 安装与支持环境： 需要 Node.js 20 或更高版本，以及所需的代理命令行工具。支持 Antigravity、Codex、Claude Code 和 DeepSeek Harness，并提供手动安装、升级和诊断方法；安装后可能需要重启 Claude Code 或 Codex。 - 路线图与许可： 计划支持通过 SSH 在不同机器之间异步委派任务。项目受 MIT 许可证保护，并受到 agy-staff 项目的启发。

item.title: Lody: Run your coding agents in parallel, safely, and share them with the team
item.description: Lody is a shared control plane for coding agents. Use the Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, or Kimi Code subscriptions you already pay for (plus any ACP-compatible agent, or an API key) and run multiple sessions on your own machines. One conversation can orchestrate sub-agents across machines, agents, and repos — parallel multi-OS tests, review-then-fix loops, and cross-repo dependency fixes. A single npx lody daemon start keeps a server or home desktop online so you can dispatch work from a phone, the web, a script, or CI. Sessions can be handed off in the team workspace (machines stay private until you share them). You can also inspect usage by member, manage PRs and CI inside a session, and check progress or permissions from the Dynamic Island.

item.title: leaf: Read papers and review diffs in the terminal, then send a selection to your coding agent
item.description: leaf is an open-source terminal reader (v0.16, MIT, written in Rust; install with curl -fsSL https://leaf.dipxsy.app | sh or cargo install leaf-reader). Give it a paper, book, doc, URL, image, diff, or GitHub PR and it lays out a clean page in the terminal — figures and tables stay in place, and every document reopens where you stopped. Select lines and press @ to send the question, file, and line context to Claude Code, Codex, or opencode running beside you. Review diffs side by side, comment, and send them to your agent or GitHub; review an agent's plan before it builds (approve / approve with notes / request changes). Also a native Rex plugin. Highlights, read-aloud, wrap-aware search, and mermaid diagrams stay in the terminal. Everything lives in one local file — no account, no sync.

item.description: - This is a Xiaohongshu recap by "AI拯救打工人（幻觉版）" of Anthropic's article "Building always-on agents," not the official text. - The note treats always-on as a user experience: the agent mostly sleeps, wakes on events or timers, writes state back after a short run, and does not burn tokens around the clock. - It recounts five primitives — Event Inbox, Timers, Memory, Permissions (including deferred tool calls), and Outbox — and the author adds that long-running capabilities may settle into the harness, with a possible loop of run, record, evaluate, distill, and improve.

item.description: - troupe is a terminal orchestrator for coding agents: one approved plan, each role in its own window, git worktree and branch, on Claude Code or Codex. - It handles parallelism by structure: file ranges live in the plan, overlaps run in series, only the orchestrator merges, and acceptance is 3–6 human-checkable Done when lines. - Humans stay at two gates — no start without an approved plan, no push without consent. item.title: Agent Memory Isn't About Storing More: Anthropic's Four Layers and Dreaming (@Smartpigai)
item.description: Smartpig (@Smartpigai) walks through Anthropic’s engineering post “The components of agent memory.” Many agent-memory projects only store chat logs, embed them, and retrieve with vector search — an approach he says overcomplicates things from the start. The core claim: memory is not about storing more, but about knowing what is worth remembering, when to recall it, and when to forget. The post splits memory into four layers: Transcripts (raw event logs), Memory Notes (experience notes that include a conclusion and why it is trustworthy), Memory Representations (a background wiki that can be navigated), and Injected Context (preload what matters; retrieve the rest; Claude Code Auto Memory loads only the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md). The technically interesting piece is Dreaming: idle compute reviews past tasks, distills reusable rules, corrects mistakes against raw transcripts, organizes a wiki, cleans contradictions, and decides what to inject next time. Results cited: CL-Bench database task, Opus 5.5 from 0.655 without memory to 0.838; in Pokémon, Sonnet 3.7 saved 413 files and earned 1 badge, while Fable 5 kept about 10 files and earned 4; on an enterprise corpus of ~350k docs / 420M tokens, search alone scored 53%, wiki+search 61%, saving ~20k tokens per question. His takeaway: the next generation of agent memory is less about RAG and more about memory lifecycle management. A reasonable engineering stack is Event Log + Structured Memory + Knowledge Wiki + Retrieval + Background Consolidation (Dreaming).

item.title: Grok Bot + Obsidian: An Automatic, Evolvable Second Brain (@Jackywine)
item.description: Jackywine (@Jackywine) recaps a month of handing his local Obsidian vault to a Grok Bot now named “Jackywine Digital Garden” (formerly “Obsidian Apprentice”; https://x.ai/bot/gdq_d-d9OCnnREs3VwGdV). A read-only diagnosis on Sept 17 found ~5,488 markdown files, nearly 40% empty stubs in the root, and ~8,000 unresolved links — the illness he named “collecting disguised as thinking.” He set four guardrails: file over app, AI output only into AI outputs/, atomic flomo imports, and sparse properties. In October he instituted a “content iron rule” (don’t write what you haven’t lived), stopped a stripped wikilink pack and an idle daily linking report, and wrote apprentice rules. On Nov 6 he renamed and split roles (flomo as memory, Obsidian as disk), walked onboarding one question at a time, wired up obsidian-cli, re-diagnosed (5,661 notes; unresolved links down to 4,747; stubs still ~43%), shipped an evergreen-note skill, and open-sourced jackywine-digital-garden-skills (7 skills, MIT). Thesis: a bot’s strength is that it can act; his most valuable decisions were what he forbade it to do. Judgment stays human. The article includes diagnosis, onboarding, apprentice, evergreen-note, related-notes, and orphan-notes prompts.
